chunks: He is the One in heaven a God, and in the earth a God, and He is the All-Wise, the All-Knowing.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean that God is a God in heaven and on earth?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited to affirm God's transcendence (Tanzih) while simultaneously acknowledging His immanence in creation, resolving the apparent paradox of being 'in' the heavens and 'on' the earth without spatial limitation. It underscores that His wisdom (Al-Hakim) and knowledge (Al-Alim) are the governing principles of both the celestial and terrestrial realms, reinforcing the concept of Tawhid in both essence and attributes.
